2027-01-01.title: The Naming of our Lord · New Year's Day
2027-01-01.alt: Feast of the Naming of our Lord, eight days after Yaldo. New Year begins. Also the World Day of Peace in the universal Church.
2027-01-01.verse: After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
theo: On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised according to the Law and given his name: Jesus, “the name given by the angel before he was conceived”. The Son of God enters fully into the covenant of his people and receives a name that is a mission: Yeshua, “the Lord saves”. As the angel told Joseph: “you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).

At the start of a new year the Church gives us not a resolution but a Name. St Peter would later proclaim: “There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved” (Acts 4:12). Every year, every plan, every fear can be placed under this Name.

St Paul's reading tells us how to begin anew: “put away your former way of life, your old self… and clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness” (Ephesians 4:22–24). A new calendar does not make a new person; Christ does. The New Year is a chance to put on Christ again.

Luke also says that Mary and Joseph brought the Child to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, offering the sacrifice of the poor, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”. The Holy Family begins every new stage by offering it to God. So may we offer this year to him.
conn: The eighth day.
Circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12) marked entry into Abraham's covenant. For Christians the eighth day became the day of the Resurrection and of the new creation.
Joshua and Jesus.
Jesus is the same name as Joshua, who led Israel into the promised land (Joshua 1:1–9). Jesus leads us into the true promised land.
The name above every name.
Paul sings that God gave Christ “the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend” (Philippians 2:9–10).
The offering of the poor.
The two birds (Leviticus 12:8) show that the Holy Family was poor. The Son of God was born among the poor.
altar: We begin the new year at the altar, where the Name of Jesus is invoked over bread and wine and he becomes present. To receive Holy Communion on the first day of the year is to place the whole year in his hands.
outline: Opening
New Year greetings: what do people usually wish for? Health, wealth, success.
Point 1 · A Name, not a wish
Jesus: “the Lord saves”. Begin the year under his Name.
Point 2 · Put on the new self
Ephesians 4: a new year needs a new heart, not only a new calendar.
Point 3 · Offer the year
Like Mary and Joseph presenting the Child, offer the year to God.
Point 4 · Peace
World Day of Peace: pray and work for peace in families and nations.
Take-home line
“Jesus, I begin this year in your Name.”
live: Begin each day with the Name
Begin each morning this year with the sign of the cross and the prayer “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me.”
One old habit to put off (Ephesians 4:22)
Name one habit of the “old self” to leave behind this year, and one virtue to put on.
Bless the house
Ask the priest to bless your home during the season of Denho, or bless it yourselves with prayer and holy water.
fathers: St Bernard of Clairvaux
The name of Jesus is light, food and medicine: “Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, a song of joy in the heart” (Sermons on the Song of Songs 15).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He praises the Name of the Son, sweet to those who love him, and the circumcision of the Lord who fulfilled the Law in himself (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 430–435
Jesus means “God saves”; the name of Jesus contains everything; it is at the heart of Christian prayer.
Catechism 527
The circumcision of Jesus is the sign of his incorporation into Abraham's descendants and prefigures Christian Baptism.
Message for the World Day of Peace
Each year on 1 January the Pope issues a message for peace; read it on vatican.va (see Papal documents).
saints: 2 Jan: Mar Baselios and Mar Gregory; name day of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis. 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, at your Naming you received the Name that saves. We begin this year in your Name: forgive our past, clothe us with the new self, bless our families and our work, and give peace to our world. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: Second Sunday after Yaldo
readings: The boy Samuel grows before the Lord
They shall mount up with wings like eagles
Here is the Lamb of God
2027-01-03.alt: Season of Yaldo–Denho. Denho, the Baptism of our Lord, is on Wednesday 6 January.
2027-01-03.verse: Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
theo: Between Yaldo and Denho the Church listens to John the Baptist. He sees Jesus coming and cries: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The Child of Bethlehem is the Lamb who will be offered for us. John adds: “I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.” Christmas joy is joined to the purpose of Christ's coming: to take away sin.

In the evening Gospel John is very practical. The crowds ask, “What then should we do?” He answers: “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.” Tax collectors must be honest; soldiers must not extort. Conversion is not only a feeling; it bears fruit in the way we use money, power and possessions.

The Old Testament readings show children growing before God: Joseph loved by his father and given a long robe; the boy Samuel growing “in the presence of the LORD”, his mother bringing him a little robe each year. Hebrews remembers Moses, who chose “to share ill-treatment with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin”.

Isaiah gives the promise for the new year: “Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary.” Those who follow the Lamb do not run on their own strength.
conn: The Lamb.
The Passover lamb (Exodus 12) and the servant “like a lamb that is led to the slaughter” (Isaiah 53:7) are fulfilled in Jesus, the Lamb of God (John 1:29; Revelation 5:6).
Robes.
Joseph's robe and Samuel's little robe are signs of a parent's love; in Baptism we are clothed with Christ (Galatians 3:27).
Love in deed.
“Let us love, not in word or speech, but in truth and action” (1 John 3:18) is the same lesson as John's “two coats”.
Moses' choice.
Moses refused Pharaoh's palace for God's people; Christ left heaven's glory for us.
altar: Before Holy Communion the priest raises the holy Mysteries; in many liturgies we hear John's words: “Behold the Lamb of God.” The One John pointed to by the Jordan is the One we receive at the altar.
outline: Opening
Ask: what did we receive at Christmas? What did we give?
Point 1 · The Lamb of God
The Child of Yaldo is the Lamb who takes away sin.
Point 2 · “What then should we do?”
Two coats, honest work, no extortion: conversion in practice.
Point 3 · Growing before God
Joseph, Samuel, Moses: let children grow in God's presence.
Point 4 · Wings like eagles
New strength for the new year for those who wait on the Lord.
Take-home line
“Behold the Lamb; and share your second coat.”
live: Share your second coat (Luke 3:11)
Give away one good item of clothing or food this week to someone who needs it.
Honest in work (Luke 3:13)
Check one area of your work or business for honesty and fairness.
Prepare for Denho
Come to the Denho Qurbono on Wednesday and renew your baptismal promises.
fathers: St Cyril of Alexandria
One Lamb died for all, to gather the whole flock of humanity to God the Father; one for all, that all might be subject to God (Commentary on John, Book 2).
St Ambrose of Milan
On “whoever has two coats”: mercy is the fullness of the virtues; it is required of all, rich and poor, according to what each has (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2).
magis: Catechism 608
John the Baptist pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world: the Suffering Servant and the Paschal Lamb.
Catechism 1434–1435
Interior conversion is expressed in fasting, prayer and almsgiving, reconciliation, and care for the poor.
Catechism 2443–2447
Love for the poor; giving to the needy is a work of justice.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan (Wednesday): Denho, the Baptism of our Lord; Holy Qurbono for the people. 7 Jan: Exaltation of St John the Baptist. 8 Jan: St Stephen, the first martyr (as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, have mercy on us. Make our conversion bear fruit in sharing, honesty and love, and renew our strength in this new year, that we may run and not be weary. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: Denho · The Baptism of our Lord
readings: You are my Son, the Beloved
Rebekah gives water at the well
The river flowing from the Temple
Draw water from the wells of salvation
Baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus
The water of rebirth and renewal
The Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan
2027-01-06.alt: Denho, the Baptism of our Lord: a day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. In many parishes the waters are solemnly blessed.
2027-01-06.verse: This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.
theo: Denho means “rising” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan the hidden Child of Bethlehem is revealed to the world. When Jesus comes up from the water, “the heavens were opened to him and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. And a voice from heaven said, ‘This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.’” For the first time the whole Holy Trinity is manifested: the Father speaks, the Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends.

John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.” Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” The sinless One goes down into the waters of repentance with sinners. He does not need to be cleansed; he cleanses the waters. The Fathers say that by his Baptism Christ sanctified the waters for our Baptism.

The Old Testament readings are full of water: Rebekah drawing water for a stranger and his camels; water filling the dry valley; Ezekiel's river flowing from the Temple, where “everything will live where the river goes”; Isaiah's promise: “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” All these streams flow into the Jordan, and from the Jordan into our baptismal font.

St Paul tells Titus: “the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all”, and God saved us “through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit”. Denho is our feast too. In Baptism the Father said to each of us, “You are my beloved child”, and the Spirit came to dwell in us. Today we renew that grace.
conn: The Trinity revealed.
Father, Son and Holy Spirit appear together at the Jordan, as the Son later sends the apostles to baptise “in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19).
The dove.
The dove over the waters recalls the Spirit hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2) and the dove of the flood (Genesis 8:11): a new creation begins.
The river of life.
Ezekiel's river (47:1–12) flows again in Revelation 22:1, “the river of the water of life… flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb”.
Baptism in the name of Jesus.
In Acts 19 Paul baptises disciples who knew only John's baptism, and the Holy Spirit comes upon them: Christian Baptism gives the Spirit.
altar: The Spirit who descended on Jesus at the Jordan descends on the bread and wine at every Holy Qurbono. The water mixed with the wine in the chalice recalls our Baptism and our union with Christ.
outline: Opening
Recall our own baptism day: who brought us, who were our godparents?
Point 1 · Denho: God revealed
The Trinity at the Jordan: the Father's voice, the Son, the Spirit.
Point 2 · Christ sanctifies the waters
The sinless One goes down among sinners; he cleanses the waters for us.
Point 3 · Wells of salvation
Rebekah, Ezekiel, Isaiah: water as God's gift of life.
Point 4 · “You are my beloved”
Baptism makes us children of God. Renew the baptismal promises.
Take-home line
“In Christ, I too am the Father's beloved child.”
live: Know your baptism day
Find out the date of your Baptism and keep it each year with a prayer of thanks.
Use holy water
Take home the blessed water of Denho; bless yourself and your children every night.
Renew the promises
Pray the Creed slowly today as the renewal of your baptismal faith.
fathers: St Gregory of Nazianzus
“Christ is baptised: let us go down with him, that we may also rise with him.” He comes to sanctify the Jordan for our sake (Oration 39, On the Holy Lights).
St Ephrem the Syrian
“Come down, my brothers, put on from the waters the Holy Spirit.” In his Hymns on the Epiphany he sings of the Lord who went down into the river and made the waters a womb of new birth.
magis: Catechism 535–537
The baptism of Jesus is his acceptance of his mission as the Suffering Servant; the Spirit and the Father's voice reveal him. Through Baptism the Christian is sacramentally assimilated to Jesus.
Catechism 1223–1225
The Lord's baptism and his Passover are the sources of Christian Baptism.
Catechism 1213
Baptism is the gateway to life in the Spirit; by it we are freed from sin and reborn as children of God.
saints: 7 Jan: Exaltation of St John the Baptist. 8 Jan: St Stephen, the first martyr. Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2027-01-06.prayer: Eternal Father, at the Jordan you revealed your beloved Son and sent your Holy Spirit upon him. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism, make us live as your beloved children, and let the river of your life flow through our homes and our Church. Amen.

2027-01-10.title: First Sunday after Denho
readings: The burning bush: I AM WHO I AM
The Lord has comforted his people
Chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world
The call of the first disciples
2027-01-10.verse: Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.
theo: After his Baptism Jesus begins his public ministry in Galilee. Matthew sees Isaiah fulfilled: “the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.” Jesus' first preaching is short: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” His first action is to call people: by the Sea of Galilee he sees Simon and Andrew, James and John at work, and says, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” “Immediately they left their nets and followed him.”

The Old Testament readings show God calling people in the middle of ordinary work. Moses was keeping his father-in-law's sheep when he saw the bush that burned and was not consumed, and heard: “Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.” God reveals his name, “I AM WHO I AM”, and sends Moses to free his people. Jacob too was a shepherd, and God blessed the work of his hands.

St Paul says that this call did not begin by the lake. God “chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love” (Ephesians 1:4). And Acts shows what the call produces: a community that “devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42).

Denho is the season of the manifestation of Christ. He is manifested not only at the Jordan, but every time someone leaves their nets and follows him. Each of us is called: to holiness, to a vocation, to bring others to Christ.
conn: Called at work.
Moses with the flock, David with the sheep, the apostles with their nets: God calls people in the middle of daily work.
Light in Galilee.
Matthew 4:16 fulfils Isaiah 9:1–2, read at Yaldo: the light born in Bethlehem now shines in Galilee.
Fishers of people.
Jeremiah 16:16 speaks of God sending “many fishermen”; Jesus turns fishermen into his messengers.
The first parish.
Acts 2:42–47 is the model of every parish: teaching, fellowship, Eucharist, prayer, sharing.
altar: The first Christians were faithful to “the breaking of bread”. The Holy Qurbono is where the call to follow Jesus is renewed each Sunday: we leave our nets for an hour and come to the One who calls us.
outline: Opening
Ask: what are the “nets” that keep us busy?
Point 1 · Light in Galilee
Jesus begins where people live and work.
Point 2 · Holy ground
Moses at the burning bush: God calls in ordinary places. Reverence before the holy.
Point 3 · Leave the nets
Immediate response. What do I need to leave to follow him?
Point 4 · A community that follows
Acts 2:42: teaching, fellowship, Qurbono, prayer. Pray for vocations.
Take-home line
“Lord, I leave my nets; I will follow you.”
live: Pray for vocations
Pray each day this week for priests, religious and missionaries from your parish.
Bring one person
Invite one person to come with you to Holy Qurbono or a prayer meeting.
Reverence in church (Exodus 3:5)
Keep silence and reverence in the church before and after Qurbono.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
He admires the obedience of the fishermen: they did not delay or say “let us go home first”, but left everything at once, as Elisha left his oxen to follow Elijah (Homilies on Matthew 14).
St Gregory of Nyssa
On the burning bush: the fire that does not consume the bush foreshadows the Virgin who bore the Light without harm, and the mystery of God's presence (Life of Moses II).
magis: Catechism 787–789
From the beginning Jesus associated his disciples with his own life; the Church is the communion with Jesus.
God reveals his name to Moses: “I AM”; the name expresses God's faithfulness.
Christus Vivit 248–258
Pope Francis on vocation: every life is a call to follow Christ and to serve.
saints: 14 Jan: St Devasahayam, martyr of Travancore. 15 Jan: Commemoration of Mary, Mother of God, for the seeds (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). 17 Jan: St Antony of Egypt.
2027-01-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of Galilee, you called fishermen to follow you and made them fishers of people. Call us again today: give us courage to leave our nets, reverence before your holiness, and joy in your Church. Raise up many vocations from our families. Amen.

2027-01-17.title: Second Sunday after Denho
readings: Jesus returns to Galilee in the power of the Spirit
I am the Lord who sanctifies you
Wisdom at the beginning of creation
He shall feed his flock in the strength of the Lord
Look to the rock from which you were hewn
Be holy, for I am holy
2027-01-17.alt: Season of Denho. The Nineveh fast (three days) is from Monday 18 to Wednesday 20 January 2027.
2027-01-17.verse: Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
theo: Philip finds Nathanael and tells him: “We have found him about whom Moses in the law and also the prophets wrote, Jesus son of Joseph from Nazareth.” Nathanael is sceptical: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue. He says: “Come and see.” That is still the best way to bring someone to Christ: not debate, but an invitation to meet him.

Jesus knows Nathanael before they meet: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Nathanael's doubt turns into faith: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” And Jesus promises more: “You will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” Jacob dreamed of a ladder between heaven and earth (Genesis 28:12); Jesus says he himself is that ladder, the meeting place of God and humanity.

Proverbs presents Wisdom, present with God “at the beginning of his work”, delighting in creation; “whoever finds me finds life”. The Fathers saw here the eternal Son, the Wisdom of God. Micah promises the ruler from Bethlehem who “shall feed his flock in the strength of the LORD”. Peter draws the consequence: “as he who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in all your conduct.”

Tomorrow the Nineveh fast begins. Jonah preached in Nineveh and the whole city repented in sackcloth and ashes. The three days of fasting prepare us for the Great Fast. Like Nathanael, we are invited to come and see; like the Ninevites, to turn back to God with our whole heart.
conn: Jacob's ladder.
John 1:51 recalls Genesis 28:12: Christ is the true Bethel, the house of God and gate of heaven.
Wisdom made flesh.
Proverbs 8:22–31 speaks of Wisdom present at creation; John 1:1–3 and Colossians 1:15–17 see in Christ the Word through whom all things were made.
The rock.
“Look to the rock from which you were hewn” (Isaiah 51:1): our faith has roots in Abraham and Sarah, and in the apostles.
Holy as God is holy.
Leviticus 22:32 (“I am the LORD; I sanctify you”) is the root of 1 Peter 1:16: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
altar: “You will see heaven opened.” At every Holy Qurbono heaven opens over the altar: the angels join our worship and the Son of Man comes down to us in his Body and Blood.
outline: Opening
Ask: who first invited you to know Jesus?
Point 1 · “Come and see”
The way of evangelisation: invitation and encounter, not argument.
Point 2 · Known by Christ
“I saw you under the fig tree.” God knows us before we know him.
Point 3 · Heaven opened
Christ is Jacob's ladder; the Qurbono is heaven on earth.
Point 4 · The Nineveh fast
Three days of fasting, prayer and repentance, as preparation for the Great Fast.
Take-home line
“Come and see.”
live: Say “Come and see”
Invite one friend, colleague or relative to Qurbono, a retreat or a prayer meeting.
Keep the Nineveh fast
Monday to Wednesday: fasting, the special prayers, and confession of sins.
Be holy in one thing (1 Peter 1:15)
Choose one area of conduct (speech, honesty, purity) to make holy this week.
fathers: St Augustine
Nathanael under the fig tree: Christ saw him before Philip called him, as he sees each of us under the shade of sin before grace calls us (Tractates on John 7).
St Athanasius of Alexandria
Proverbs 8 speaks of the Son, the Wisdom of the Father, through whom all things were made, and who became man for our sake (Against the Arians II).
magis: Evangelii Gaudium 127–129
Evangelisation person to person: a friendly conversation that invites the other to encounter Christ.
Catechism 1438
Seasons of penance in the liturgical year are intense moments of the Church's penitential practice.
Catechism 2013–2014
All the faithful are called to the fullness of Christian life and to holiness.
saints: 17 Jan: St Antony of Egypt. 18–20 Jan: the Nineveh fast. 18–25 Jan: the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. 20 Jan: St Sebastian. 21 Jan: St Agnes.
2027-01-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw Nathanael under the fig tree and opened heaven before him. Help us to say “Come and see” to those who do not know you, and in these days of the Nineveh fast turn our hearts back to you, that we may be holy as you are holy. Amen.

2027-01-24.title: Kohne Sunday · Commemoration of the Departed Priests
readings: Aaron anointed for an everlasting covenant
Paul's farewell to the elders of Ephesus
2027-01-24.alt: Kohne Sunday: the Church remembers the priests who have died. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was also Catholicos Day.
2027-01-24.verse: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
theo: Before the Great Fast the Malankara Church keeps three Sundays of remembrance. The first is Kohne Sunday, the commemoration of the departed priests (kohne in Syriac). We remember the bishops and priests who baptised us, taught us, absolved our sins, celebrated the Holy Qurbono for us, and buried our dead. Hebrews tells us: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.”

The readings recall the death of Israel's great servants. Aaron, the first high priest, dies on Mount Hor, and Moses places his vestments on his son Eleazar (Numbers 20:28): the priesthood continues though the priest dies. Joshua dies after leading the people into the land. Sirach remembers Aaron anointed “for an everlasting covenant… to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name” (Sirach 45:15).

In Acts Paul says farewell to the elders of Ephesus: “Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.” And he reminds them of the Lord's words: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” The Gospel asks the question every priest will be asked: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time? Blessed is that servant whom his master will find at work when he arrives.”

We pray today for the departed priests, that the Lord who called them may forgive their weaknesses and say to them: “Well done, good servant!” (Luke 19:17). And we pray for our living priests, and for new vocations. “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever” (Hebrews 13:8): priests pass, but the one High Priest remains.
conn: Vestments passed on.
Aaron's garments placed on Eleazar (Numbers 20:28): the priesthood does not die with the priest. In the Church the one priesthood of Christ continues through every generation.
The faithful servant.
Luke 19 and Matthew 24: priests are stewards, not owners; they will give an account.
Paul's farewell.
Acts 20 is the model of a pastor's last words: I did not shrink from declaring the whole purpose of God; I coveted no one's silver or gold.
One High Priest.
Hebrews 13:8–16: Christ the same yesterday, today and for ever; our sacrifice of praise continues his.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono offered today in the world is offered by hands that will one day be still. Through them the one Priest, Christ, offers his one sacrifice. Today we offer the Qurbono for the priests who once stood at this altar for us.
outline: Opening
Name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you, buried your parents.
Point 1 · Remember your leaders
Gratitude for the priests who served us.
Point 2 · The priesthood continues
Aaron's vestments on Eleazar: Christ's priesthood outlives every priest.
Point 3 · Faithful stewards
The faithful and wise servant: a word for priests and for every Christian steward.
Point 4 · Pray for priests
For the departed, for the living, for vocations.
Take-home line
“Remember them, and imitate their faith.”
live: Pray for departed priests
Pray by name for the priests who served your family, living and dead.
Thank your parish priest
Tell your parish priest one thing you are grateful for.
Pray for vocations
Pray daily for one young person from your parish to answer God's call.
fathers: St John Chrysostom

On the priesthood: the priest stands at the altar as a minister of heavenly things; the dignity is great, and so is the responsibility, for he will answer for the souls entrusted to him (On the Priesthood III).
St Gregory the Great
The good shepherd is known by his care for the flock: he must be near to each by compassion and above all by contemplation (Pastoral Rule II).
magis: Presbyterorum Ordinis 2–3
Priests share in the priesthood of Christ; taken from among the people, they are set apart for the people, to offer sacrifice and forgive sins in Christ's name.
Catechism 1547–1553
The ministerial priesthood is at the service of the common priesthood; the priest acts in the person of Christ the Head.
Catechism 1032
The Church prays and offers the Eucharistic sacrifice for the dead.
saints: 25 Jan: the Conversion of St Paul; the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity ends. 26 Jan: Republic Day of India. 28 Jan: St Thomas Aquinas. 31 Jan: St John Bosco.
2027-01-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal High Priest, we remember before you the bishops and priests who served your people and have gone to their rest. Forgive their weaknesses, reward their labours, and give them a place of light. Keep our living priests faithful, and raise up new labourers for your harvest. Amen.

2027-01-31.title: Aneede Sunday · Commemoration of the Departed Faithful
readings: Jacob is gathered to his people
New heavens and a new earth
We will be with the Lord for ever
The dead will hear the voice of the Son of God
2027-01-31.alt: Aneede Sunday: the Church remembers all the faithful departed. The Great Fast begins next Sunday. (In 2025–26 this Sunday was also Malankara Catholic Children's League Day.)
2027-01-31.verse: Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
theo: Last Sunday we remembered the departed priests; today, Aneede Sunday, we remember all the faithful departed: our parents and grandparents, brothers and sisters, children and friends. The Church does not forget them. Before we enter the Great Fast, we gather them in prayer, because Lent leads to Easter, the victory of Christ over death.

Jesus says: “The hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live… all who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out.” St Paul writes to the Thessalonians so “that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.” Christian grief is real, but it is grief with hope: “so we will be with the Lord forever.”

The reading from 2 Maccabees shows that God's people prayed for the dead even before Christ. Judas Maccabeus took up a collection for a sin offering for the fallen, “for if he were not expecting that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead”. From the beginning the Church has prayed for the departed and offered the Holy Qurbono for them, that they may be purified and enter the joy of God.

The evening Gospel reminds us how we will be judged: “I was hungry and you gave me food… just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.” The best way to honour our dead is to pray for them and to live in such a way that, when our turn comes, we too may hear: “Come, you that are blessed by my Father.”
conn: Gathered to his people.
Jacob “breathed his last, and was gathered to his people” (Genesis 49:33): death is a gathering, not an ending.
Prayer for the dead.
2 Maccabees 12:45 is the Old Testament root of the Church's prayer for the departed (CCC 1032).
Hezekiah's song.
“You have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back” (Isaiah 38:17): God's mercy reaches beyond death.
New heavens and a new earth.
2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1: our hope is not only for souls but for a renewed creation and the resurrection of the body.
altar: In every Holy Qurbono, in the Thubden, the Church remembers the faithful departed by name. Today we offer the Qurbono for all our dead: the Body and Blood of the risen Lord are the pledge of their resurrection and ours.
outline: Opening
Invite the people to name silently those they have lost.
Point 1 · Grief with hope
1 Thessalonians 4: not as those who have no hope.
Point 2 · Why we pray for the dead
2 Maccabees 12; the Church's tradition; the Qurbono for the departed.
Point 3 · Judged on love
Matthew 25: the hungry, the stranger, the sick, the prisoner.
Point 4 · Preparing for the Fast
Lent is the journey to the Resurrection.
Take-home line
“We will be with the Lord forever.”
live: Pray for your dead
Write the names of your departed family members and pray for them each day this week; offer a Qurbono for them.
Visit the cemetery
Visit the graves of your family, clean them, and pray there.
Do one work of mercy (Matthew 25)
Feed, visit or clothe someone this week in memory of a departed loved one.
fathers: St Augustine
His mother Monica asked as she was dying: “Lay this body anywhere; only this I ask of you, that you remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you may be” (Confessions IX, 11).
St John Chrysostom
“Let us help and commemorate them… Why would you doubt that our offerings for the dead bring them some consolation?” (Homilies on 1 Corinthians 41).
magis: Catechism 1030–1032
Those who die in God's grace but still imperfectly purified undergo purification; the Church commends prayer, the Eucharistic sacrifice, almsgiving and works of penance for them.
Catechism 1680–1690
The Christian funeral and the communion of saints with the departed.
Lumen Gentium 49–50
The union of the pilgrim Church with those who have died in Christ is not broken, but strengthened by the sharing of spiritual goods.
saints: 31 Jan: St John Bosco. 2 Feb (Tuesday): Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple. 3 Feb: Mar Simon and Morth Hanna (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). 4 Feb: St John de Britto.
2027-01-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the resurrection and the life. Remember all our departed brothers and sisters, our parents, relatives, friends and benefactors, and those whom no one remembers. Forgive their sins, give them eternal rest, and let perpetual light shine upon them. Amen.

quick: Jesus means “the Lord saves”.
Begin the year with a Name, not just a wish.
Put off the old self and put on the new.
2027-01-01.action: Name one old habit to leave behind and one virtue to put on this year.
2027-01-01.question: Under whose name will I live this year?
2027-01-01.special: The Naming of our Lord and New Year's Day. World Day of Peace.
illus: In many Kerala homes the first thing written in a new notebook or account book is a cross, or “Jesus” at the top of the first page. It is a small act of faith: everything that follows is placed under his Name.

family.explain: When Jesus was eight days old, Mary and Joseph gave him the name the angel had told them: Jesus, which means “God saves”.
family.intention: We offer this new year to Jesus and pray for peace in our family and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing will each of us try to do this year?”

catechism: Prayer in the name of Jesus.
kidsaint: A bishop in Caesarea who built a whole “new city” for the poor and sick, with hospitals and kitchens. Lesson: begin the new year by helping someone in need.
term: Jesus (Yeshua) means “the Lord saves”. Christians pray in this Name, bow at it, and begin their work under it. The ancient Jesus Prayer is: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
termMore: Jewish boys were circumcised and named on the eighth day (Leviticus 12:3). The feast falls on 1 January, the octave day of Yaldo, which is also the civil New Year.

quick: The Child of Bethlehem is the Lamb of God.
Conversion bears fruit: share your second coat.
Those who wait for the Lord renew their strength.
2027-01-03.action: Give away one good item of clothing or food this week.
2027-01-03.question: What is my “second coat” that someone else needs?
2027-01-03.special: Second Sunday after Yaldo. Announce Denho on Wednesday 6 January, a day of obligation.
illus: After Christmas many Kerala homes have cupboards full of new clothes. One parish asks families to bring one good garment to church on the Sunday after Christmas for the poor. The pile at the door is John the Baptist's sermon in action.

family.explain: John the Baptist said: if you have two shirts, give one away. And he pointed to Jesus and said: “Look, the Lamb of God!”
family.intention: We pray for people who are cold or hungry this January.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week?”

kidsaint: A priest from Kainakary in Kerala who started schools beside churches so that every child could learn, founded religious congregations and printed books. Lesson: learning is a gift from God; use it to help others.
term: John the Baptist's name for Jesus (John 1:29). It recalls the Passover lamb and the Suffering Servant of Isaiah: Jesus gives his life to take away the sin of the world.
termMore: The days from Christmas to the Baptism of the Lord unfold one mystery: God revealed in Christ, to the shepherds, to the Magi, and at the Jordan.

quick: Denho: at the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed.
Christ, who has no sin, sanctifies the waters for our Baptism.
In Baptism the Father calls each of us “my beloved child”.
2027-01-06.action: Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-01-06.question: Do I live as the Father's beloved child?
2027-01-06.special: Denho, the Baptism of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: In old Kerala Christian homes the date of Baptism was written inside the family Bible, beside the date of birth. Many grandparents knew it better than their birthday. Denho reminds us that the second birth matters even more than the first.

family.explain: Jesus was baptised by John in the river Jordan. Heaven opened, the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and the Father said: “This is my beloved Son.” At our Baptism God said the same about us!
family.intention: We thank God for our Baptism and pray for our godparents.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptised, and who our godparents are?”

kidsaint: He lived in the desert, called people to change their hearts, and had the joy of baptising Jesus. He said: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” Lesson: point others to Jesus, not to yourself.
term: Syriac for “rising” or “dawn”: the manifestation of Christ at his Baptism in the Jordan, 6 January. In the Malankara tradition the waters are solemnly blessed on this feast, and the faithful take the blessed water home.
termMore: From the early centuries the Eastern Churches celebrated on 6 January the manifestation of Christ, above all his Baptism. The season of Denho continues until the Great Fast.

quick: Jesus begins his mission by calling people.
God calls in the middle of ordinary work.
Leave the nets: following Christ needs a real decision.
2027-01-10.action: Invite one person to Holy Qurbono or a prayer meeting this week.
2027-01-10.question: What nets do I need to leave to follow Jesus more closely?
illus: Many priests and sisters from Kerala's coastal parishes grew up in fishing families. More than one says the call came while helping father mend the nets. The Gospel of the lake keeps happening in Kerala.

family.explain: Jesus walked by the lake and saw fishermen. He said: “Follow me!” They left their nets at once and went with him.
family.intention: We pray for vocations to the priesthood and religious life from our family and parish.
family.ask: Ask: “What is Jesus asking our family to do for him?”

catechism: Jesus calls disciples into communion with him.
Every person is called to love and serve.
kidsaint: Simon was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. When Jesus called him, he left his boat and nets and followed him. Jesus made him the leader of the apostles. Lesson: say yes quickly when Jesus calls.
term: The season after the Baptism of the Lord, until the Great Fast. Its Sundays show Christ revealed in his ministry: calling disciples, teaching, and showing his glory.
termMore: At the burning bush Moses removed his sandals (Exodus 3:5). In many Eastern churches the faithful still remove their sandals before entering the sanctuary area.

quick: “Come and see”: the best way to bring someone to Christ.
Christ is the ladder between heaven and earth.
The Nineveh fast begins tomorrow: return to God.
2027-01-17.action: Invite one person to “come and see” this week.
2027-01-17.question: Whom can I invite to come and see Jesus?
2027-01-17.special: Second Sunday after Denho. Remind the faithful: the Nineveh fast (three days) is from Monday 18 to Wednesday 20 January, with the special prayers and abstinence.
illus: A young engineer in the Gulf stopped going to church for years. A colleague never argued with him, but every Friday said, “Come with me to Qurbono, just once.” One day he came, and he still goes. “Come and see” is still how faith spreads.

family.explain: Philip told Nathanael about Jesus. Nathanael was not sure, so Philip said: “Come and see!” When Nathanael met Jesus, he believed.
family.intention: We pray for friends and relatives who have drifted away from the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep the Nineveh fast together as a family?”

catechism: Many forms of penance; the Nineveh fast.
kidsaint: A young man who heard the Gospel “sell what you own and give to the poor” and did it. He went to pray in the desert, and many came to learn from him. Lesson: when you hear God's Word, do it.
term: Three days of fasting before the Great Fast, recalling the repentance of Nineveh at Jonah's preaching (Jonah 3). The Malankara lectionary asks for special prayers, prostrations and abstinence in these days.
termMore: Jesus himself said “Come and see” to his first disciples (John 1:39); Philip repeats it to Nathanael. Faith passes from friend to friend.

quick: Kohne Sunday: we remember the departed priests.
The priesthood continues: Christ is the one High Priest.
“Remember your leaders and imitate their faith.”
2027-01-24.action: Pray by name for the priests who served your family.
2027-01-24.question: Which priest helped my faith most, and how can I thank God for him?
2027-01-24.special: Kohne Sunday, commemoration of the departed priests. (In 2025–26 also Catholicos Day; check the 2026–27 lectionary for collections.)
illus: In many Kerala parishes the tombs of former vicars lie near the church door. On Kohne Sunday the people light candles there after Qurbono. Some of those priests baptised the grandparents of today's children.

family.explain: Priests bring us Jesus in the Holy Qurbono and in Confession. Today we thank God for priests who have died and pray that they are happy with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the priests who have died, for our parish priest, and for new vocations.
family.ask: Ask: “Which priest baptised each of us? Let us pray for him.”

catechism: Purification after death and prayer for the dead.
kidsaint: A priest in Turin who gathered poor boys from the streets, taught them a trade, played with them and led them to Jesus. Lesson: priests are fathers who care for us; pray for them.
term: Kohne is Syriac for “priests”. The first of three Sundays of remembrance before the Great Fast: departed priests (Kohne), all the departed faithful (Aneede), then the Fast begins with Kothine (Cana) Sunday.
termMore: Before entering the Great Fast, the Church remembers her dead: it is a reminder that Lent is a journey towards Easter, the victory over death.

quick: Aneede Sunday: we remember all the faithful departed.
Christian grief has hope: we will be with the Lord for ever.
We will be judged on love: what we did for the least.
2027-01-31.action: Offer a Qurbono and pray daily this week for your departed family members.
2027-01-31.question: How am I preparing for my own meeting with the Lord?
2027-01-31.special: Aneede Sunday, commemoration of the faithful departed. Announce the beginning of the Great Fast with Kothine Sunday (7 February) and the Shubkono on Monday 8 February.
illus: In Kerala families the name of a departed parent is written in the parish register for the annual Qurbono, and the family gathers every year on that day. Love does not stop at the grave; it becomes prayer.

family.explain: When people we love die, we are sad. But Jesus rose from the dead, and he will raise them too. We pray for them so that they may be happy with God.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family has gone to God? Let us tell one good memory of them.”

kidsaint: The mother of St Augustine, who prayed for her son for many years until he came back to God. Before she died she asked him only to remember her at the altar. Lesson: pray for those you love, living and dead.
term: Aneede is Syriac for “the departed”. On the Sunday before the Great Fast the Malankara Church remembers all the faithful departed, after remembering the departed priests on Kohne Sunday.
termMore: Why do we pray for the dead?
Because love does not end with death, and because the dead who still need purification can be helped by the prayers and offerings of the living (2 Maccabees 12:45; CCC 1032).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed New Year to all of you! On this first day of the year, the Church celebrates the Naming of our Lord. Eight days after his birth, the Child was circumcised and given the name the angel had announced: Jesus.

In Hebrew, Jesus means “the Lord saves”. The angel told Joseph: “you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” So on New Year's Day the Church does not give us a list of resolutions; she gives us a Name. St Peter says: “There is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.”

St Paul tells us what a real new beginning looks like: put away the old self, and clothe yourselves with the new self, created in the likeness of God. A new calendar does not make a new person. Only Christ makes us new. Let each of us name one old habit to put off, and one virtue to put on, this year.

And like Mary and Joseph, who brought the Child to offer him to the Lord, let us offer this whole year to God: our families, our work, our health, our plans. Today is also the World Day of Peace. May the Prince of Peace give peace to our homes and to our world. Jesus, we begin this year in your Name. Amen.
kids: Children, happy New Year! Today we remember the day baby Jesus got his name. Do you know what “Jesus” means? “God saves!”
Mary and Joseph gave him that name because an angel told them to. Jesus came to save us and help us be good.
This year, let's start every day by saying: “Jesus, I love you!” Let's say it together now: “Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, we are still in the light of Christmas, and today John the Baptist points to the Child of Bethlehem and says: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The baby in the manger came for a purpose: to give his life for us, as the Passover lamb was given for Israel.

In the evening Gospel the crowds ask John: “What then should we do?” His answer is very simple. “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; whoever has food must do likewise.” To tax collectors: be honest. To soldiers: do not extort. Conversion is not a beautiful feeling; it is a changed way of using what we have.

After Christmas many of us have more than enough: new clothes, sweets, gifts. John asks: where is your second coat? Who needs it? Our readings also show children growing up close to God: Samuel growing in the presence of the Lord, his mother bringing him a little robe each year. Let us help our children grow like that.

And as the new year begins, Isaiah promises: “Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” On Wednesday we celebrate Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Come, renew your own baptism, and follow the Lamb. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was Jesus' cousin. When he saw Jesus coming, he said: “Look! The Lamb of God!” He meant that Jesus came to take away all our sins.
People asked John: “What should we do?” He said: “If you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none.”
Do you have a toy or a shirt you could share? Let's say: “Like John, I will share!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Denho, the feast of the manifestation of the Lord. The Child of Bethlehem, hidden for thirty years in Nazareth, comes to the Jordan and is revealed to the world. When he comes up out of the water, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice says: “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”

John did not want to baptise him: “I need to be baptised by you!” But Jesus went down into the water with sinners. Why? He had no sin to wash away. The Fathers answer: he went down to make the waters holy for us. The Jordan became the source of every baptismal font in the world.

Our Old Testament readings are full of water: Rebekah at the well, a river flowing from the Temple bringing life wherever it goes, Isaiah's joyful promise: “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” In our Baptism we drank from those wells. And the same voice spoke over each of us: “You are my beloved child.”

Today, as the waters are blessed, let us renew our baptismal promises with faith. Take the blessed water home; bless your children with it each night. Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it every year. Live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember the day Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. When he came out of the water, heaven opened!
The Holy Spirit came down like a white dove, and God the Father said: “This is my beloved Son!” Father, Son and Holy Spirit, all together.
When you were baptised, God said: “You are my beloved child!” Do you know your baptism day? Ask your parents tonight! Let's say: “I am God's beloved child!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Wednesday we celebrated Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Now Jesus begins his work. He goes to Galilee, a region of ordinary working people, and begins to preach: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” And the first thing he does is call people.

He walks by the lake and sees fishermen at work: Simon and Andrew casting their nets, James and John mending theirs. He says: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him. No delay, no long negotiation.

God always calls people at work. Moses was looking after sheep when he saw the burning bush and heard: “Remove your sandals, for the place where you stand is holy ground.” The ordinary place of his work became holy because God was there. Your kitchen, your office, your field can become holy ground too.

What are your nets? Your phone, your worries, your ambitions, your comforts? Jesus does not always ask us to leave our jobs, but he always asks us to put him first. And some of our young people he calls to leave everything for the priesthood or religious life. Let us pray for them, and let us answer him: “Lord, I will follow you.” Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus walked by a big lake and saw fishermen catching fish. He said: “Come, follow me! I will make you fishers of people!”
The fishermen left their nets straight away and went with Jesus. They became his friends, the apostles.
Jesus calls you too: to be his friend and bring others to him. Let's say: “Jesus, I will follow you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's Gospel tells how one friend brought another to Jesus. Philip found Nathanael and said: “We have found the one Moses and the prophets wrote about: Jesus of Nazareth.” Nathanael laughed: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?”

Philip did not argue. He simply said: “Come and see.” That is still the best way to bring people to Christ. Not long debates, not pressure, but an invitation: come and see. Come to Qurbono with me. Come to the prayer meeting. Meet him yourself.

When Nathanael came, Jesus said: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Jesus knew him already. Nathanael's doubt melted: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!” And Jesus promised: “You will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” He is Jacob's ladder; in him heaven and earth meet. At this altar, today, heaven opens.

Tomorrow the Nineveh fast begins. When Jonah preached, the whole city turned back to God. Let us keep these three days well: fasting, the special prayers, a good Confession. And this week, let each of us say to one person: “Come and see.” Amen.
kids: Children, Philip met Jesus and was so happy! He ran to his friend Nathanael and said: “Come and see Jesus!”
Nathanael came, and Jesus said: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Jesus knew him already! Nathanael believed.
Jesus knows you too, and loves you. Who can you invite to come and meet Jesus? Let's say: “Come and see!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Kohne Sunday, when our Church remembers the priests who have died. Think for a moment of the priests in your own life: the one who baptised you, who gave you your First Holy Communion, who heard your confessions, who blessed your marriage, who buried your parents. Many of them are now with the Lord.

The letter to the Hebrews says: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” We remember them with gratitude. They were human, with weaknesses like ours, but through their hands Christ gave us his Body and Blood and his forgiveness.

Our reading from Numbers tells how Aaron, the first high priest, died, and Moses placed his vestments on his son Eleazar. The priest dies; the priesthood continues. For Christ is the one eternal High Priest, “the same yesterday and today and forever”. And the Gospel asks every priest one question: were you a faithful and wise servant, giving God's household their food at the proper time?

Today let us offer this Qurbono for our departed priests, that the Lord may say to them: “Well done, good servant.” Let us thank and support our living priests. And let us pray that from our families God may call new priests, to stand at this altar when we are gone. Amen.
kids: Children, who baptised you? A priest! Who gives you Jesus in Holy Communion? A priest!
Today we remember priests who have died and gone to Jesus. We thank God for them and pray that they are happy in heaven.
Let's pray for our parish priest too. Maybe one day God will call one of you to be a priest or sister! Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for our priests!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we remembered our departed priests. Today, Aneede Sunday, we remember all our faithful departed. Let us take a moment of silence and bring to mind those we have lost: a father, a mother, a husband, a wife, a child, a friend.

St Paul writes: we do not want you to grieve “as others do who have no hope”. He does not say “do not grieve”. Jesus himself wept at the tomb of his friend. But our grief has hope, because Christ is risen. Jesus says: “All who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out.” One day our dead will hear that voice.

Why do we pray for the dead? Our reading from Maccabees says: if Judas had not believed in the resurrection, it would have been foolish to pray for the fallen. The Church has always prayed and offered the Holy Qurbono for the departed, that they may be purified and enter fully into God's joy. St Monica asked her son Augustine only one thing before she died: “Remember me at the altar of the Lord.”

And the evening Gospel reminds us how we ourselves will be judged: “I was hungry and you gave me food… as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.” Next Sunday the Great Fast begins. Let us enter it remembering that life is short, that love is what remains, and that we too are walking towards the Lord. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, do you have a grandpa or grandma who has gone to God? Today we remember all the people we love who have died.
We feel sad, but we also have hope, because Jesus rose from the dead and he will bring them to new life.
Tonight, pray for them by name. Let's say: “Jesus, keep them happy with you in heaven!”

intro: Theme: “Begin the year in the name of Jesus.”
On the eighth day the Child received the name the angel had given: Jesus, “God saves”. We begin the new year not with luck or fear but with a name: the name above every name.

points.h: The name that reveals who he is
sub: At the burning bush God revealed his name to Moses: a name to be remembered for all generations.
In Jesus that name becomes a person: “God saves”.
Mary and Joseph obey the angel: they give the name God chose.
q: This is my name forever, and this my title for all generations.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Say the name of Jesus with reverence; never use it carelessly.

points.h: There is no other saving name
sub: The prophets promised: whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Peter proclaimed: there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.
In every need of the coming year, call on this name with faith.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Make the short prayer “Jesus, I trust in you” your companion this year.

points.h: A new year, a new self
sub: The priests of Israel blessed the people by placing God's name upon them.
Mary and Joseph presented the Child to the Lord; we present this new year to him.
St Paul tells us to put off the old self and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness.
q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.
points.apply: Write one resolution for the year that will make you more like Christ, and offer it at the altar today.

concl: Whatever this year brings, it is placed under the name of Jesus.
Let us begin it blessed, cleansed and renewed, calling on the name that saves.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with the words of Numbers 6:24–26 at the start of each month this year.

intro: John the Baptist points away from himself to Jesus: “Here is the Lamb of God.” He also tells ordinary people how to prepare for him: by concrete repentance in daily life.

sub: Isaiah saw a silent Servant led like a lamb to the slaughter.
John recognises Jesus as the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world.
The Church calls Christ the Lamb in her liturgy; in the Holy Qurbono we receive the Lamb who was sacrificed for us.
q: Like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Look at the Holy Mysteries at the elevation and say in your heart: “Lamb of God, have mercy on me.”

sub: The crowds ask: “What then should we do?”
John's answers are practical: share your coat and food; collect only what is just; do not threaten or accuse falsely.
Isaiah too: cease to do evil, learn to do good, defend the orphan and the widow.
q: Cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.
And the crowds asked him, “What then should we do?” In reply he said to them, “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.”
points.apply: Give away one good garment or one day's food to someone in need this week.

sub: The boy Samuel grew in favour with God and people while serving in the Temple.
John saw the Spirit descend and testified: “This is the Son of God.”
Every Christian is called to grow in faith and to bear witness, not to himself, but to Christ.
q: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favor with the LORD and with the people.
And I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.
points.apply: Speak of Jesus simply to one person this week: what he means to you.

concl: John's whole life is a finger pointing to Christ.
Let our lives too say to others: “Behold the Lamb of God.”
2027-01-03.resolve: Pray each night this week: “Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.”

intro: Theme: “The heavens opened: the Son, the Spirit, the Father, and our Baptism.”
Denho means “dawning” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan Jesus is revealed as the beloved Son, the Spirit rests on him, and the Father speaks. Today we also remember our own Baptism.

points.h: The sinless One enters our waters
sub: John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.”
Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to fulfil all righteousness”: he stands with sinners.
The Fathers say: he did not need the waters to make him holy; he made the waters holy for us.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
But Jesus answered him, “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he consented.
points.apply: Thank God for the humility of Christ, who stands in line with sinners.

sub: The heavens are torn apart: God's distance is overcome.
The Spirit descends like a dove; the Father's voice declares the beloved Son.
Isaiah's servant, filled with the Spirit, is revealed: Jesus is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.

And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross today slowly, thinking of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

points.h: Our Baptism: drawing water from the wells of salvation
sub: Isaiah promised joy from the wells of salvation.
In Baptism the same Spirit came upon us; in Chrismation we were sealed with holy Myron.
St Paul's disciples at Ephesus received the Spirit when hands were laid on them.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
He saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it every year.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened; at our Baptism heaven opened for us.
Let us live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Spirit, following the Son.
2027-01-06.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises at home this week: reject sin and profess the Creed.

intro: After his Baptism Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee. Light dawns on a land in darkness, and ordinary fishermen hear a call that changes their lives. The same call reaches us.

sub: Jesus begins not in Jerusalem but in “Galilee of the Gentiles”, a mixed and despised region.
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled: a light for the nations.
Christ still begins where people sit in darkness: in our struggles and our neighbourhoods.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Pray for one person you know who is in darkness: illness, addiction, despair.

sub: God called Moses by name from the bush, and he answered: “Here I am.”
Jesus calls fishermen at their work: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
They leave their nets “immediately”: a call delayed is often a call lost.
q: God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Ask: what “net” holds me back from following Jesus more closely? Leave it this week.

points.h: A community born of the call
sub: Those who answered became the first Church: teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer.
God heals the brokenhearted and gathers his people.
Every call to follow Christ is also a call into his Church.
q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
points.apply: Join one parish activity (prayer group, catechism, charity) this month. Pray for vocations.

concl: The Light has come, the call has been given, and the community is gathered.
Let us answer like Moses, “Here I am”, and like the apostles, leave our nets to follow him.
2027-01-10.resolve: Pray daily this week for priestly and religious vocations from your parish.

intro: Philip finds Nathanael and tells him about Jesus. Nathanael doubts: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue; he invites: “Come and see.” Faith grows through encounter.

sub: Nathanael's question is honest; God is not afraid of our questions.
Wisdom promises that those who seek diligently will find.
The best answer to doubt is an invitation to meet Christ in Scripture, in the Qurbono and in a living community.
q: I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me.
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
points.apply: Invite one person who has drifted away to come with you to Sunday Qurbono.

sub: Jesus praises Nathanael: “an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.”
God says: “I am the LORD; I sanctify you”: holiness begins with an honest heart.
Jesus already knew Nathanael under the fig tree; nothing is hidden from him.
q: You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be sanctified among the people of Israel: I am the LORD; I sanctify you.
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said of him, “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!”
points.apply: Remove one falsehood from your life this week: a lie, a pretence, a double life.

points.h: Heaven opened: Christ is the ladder
sub: Jacob dreamed of a ladder with angels ascending and descending.
Jesus says: you will see heaven opened and angels on the Son of Man: he is the meeting place of heaven and earth.
In the Holy Qurbono heaven opens; we join the angels in praise.
q: And he dreamed that there was a ladder set up on the earth, the top of it reaching to heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
points.apply: At the Sanctus, remember that you are singing with the angels.

concl: Nathanael moved from doubt to confession: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!”
Let us come and see, let our hearts be without deceit, and find in Christ the open heaven.
2027-01-17.resolve: Read John 1:35–51 slowly once this week and ask: where is Jesus inviting me to “come and see”?

intro: Theme: “Remembering the priests who served us.”
On Kohne Sunday the Church remembers her departed priests. We thank God for them, we pray for them, and we reflect on the gift of the priesthood that continues among us.

sub: On Mount Hor Moses took Aaron's vestments and put them on Eleazar: the ministry continues after death.
Every priest is taken from among the people and appointed for the people, to offer gifts and sacrifices.
The priests who baptised us, absolved us and fed us with the Eucharist have handed on Christ's priesthood to the next generation.
q: Moses stripped Aaron of his vestments, and put them on his son Eleazar; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain.
Every high priest chosen from among mortals is put in charge of things pertaining to God on their behalf, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
points.apply: Remember by name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you or buried your loved ones.

points.h: Faithful stewards of the Master's gift
sub: Aaron was anointed to minister to the Lord and bless the people in his name.
In the parable of the pounds, the faithful servant is praised for trading with what he received.
Priests are judged by faithfulness, not success; so are all of us in our vocations.
q: Moses ordained him, and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and for his descendants … to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name.
He said to him, “Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.”
points.apply: Encourage a priest this week with a word of thanks, and pray for one who is struggling.

sub: Judas Maccabeus offered sacrifice for the dead, “a holy and pious thought”.
The Church prays for the faithful departed, that they may be purified and enter God's rest.
Our prayers and Holy Qurbono offered for departed priests are an act of gratitude and charity.
q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
Blessed are the dead who from now on die in the Lord. “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds follow them.”
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered, or pray a Rosary, for a departed priest.

concl: The priests we remember today gave their lives so that Christ might be present among us.
Let us thank God for them, pray for their eternal rest, and pray that the Lord will send good and holy priests to his Church.
2027-01-24.resolve: Visit the grave of a priest in your parish cemetery and pray for him.

intro: On Aneede Sunday we remember all our departed: parents, grandparents, friends. We do not come as people without hope. We come to pray for them and to learn from them how to live.

points.h: In Christ, death is a passage to life
sub: Jacob ended his blessing, breathed his last and was “gathered to his people”.
Jesus promises: whoever hears his word and believes has already passed from death to life.
Our departed are not lost; they are on the way home, and we pray that they reach it.
q: When Jacob ended his charge to his sons, he drew up his feet into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
points.apply: Name your departed loved ones in prayer each day this week.

sub: Hezekiah, facing death, turned to God and found mercy.
St Paul does not forbid grief; he forbids grief without hope.
The Church prays for the dead, that they may be purified and see God; this is an act of love (CCC 1032).
q: Surely it was for my welfare that I had great bitterness; but you have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

We do not want you to be uninformed … about those who have died, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope. For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have died.
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered for your departed, and visit the cemetery with your family.

points.h: We will be judged by love
sub: At the last judgment the King asks about the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner.
Proverbs says kindness to the poor is a loan to the Lord.
The best way to honour our dead is to live the works of mercy they taught us.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy this week in memory of a departed loved one.

concl: The dead hear the voice of the Son of God; those who have done good will rise to life.
Let us pray for our departed with faith and live with charity, so that one day we may meet them in the Father's house.
2027-01-31.resolve: Pray “Eternal rest grant to them, O Lord” for the departed after each meal this week.
